propositions: A drainer process dying between lock acquire and release creates a permanent 0-byte orphan lock file with no owner stamp that blocks all future drain attempts with FileExistsError, causing enrichment to silently skip indefinitely.
The drain lock lacks staleness adjudication, stale-reclaim logic, and bounded retry—unlike the store's mkdir write lock—so a leaked lock has no recovery path and no visibility.
The fix extracts a shared staleness decision core into lock_owner._stamp_is_stale, writes v2 owner stamps on acquire, and implements bounded stale-file reclaim with one retry on collision.
Unrecognised/unstamped drain lock stamps are treated as non-proof and fall to a 1h wall-clock ceiling for reclaimability, while mkdir locks preserve legacy v2-or-false routing.
Stale drain locks are unlinked and reclaimed with a single bounded retry; a second FileExistsError means a competing drainer won and drain skips with WARNING naming the holder.
The drain log moves from INFO to WARNING on skip, drain() acquires with stamped v2 ownership, and doctor's drain leg reports real staleness verdicts instead of not-assessable.
